page: Microsoft Azure D4pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an ARM-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores running at 3.4 GHz with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations show average performance across most standard operations. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests yield scores of 2073.38 and 8274.75 respectively, while the Geekbench multi-core score reaches 5596.0. Notably, the instance exhibits strong single-threaded gzip compression at 33.1 GB/sec. However, cryptographic and specialized vector instruction performance is weak, as evidenced by a poor PassMark CPU encryption score of 748.72 and a weak ray tracing score. Memory bandwidth is solid, with cached read speeds reaching 454.75 GB/sec.

Built on ARM architecture, the D4pds_v6 offers a highly resource-dense profile that delivers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that do not rely heavily on x86-specific instruction sets. The combination of dedicated ARM cores, balanced memory, and local NVMe storage makes this instance suitable for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations such as Redis caching. It is less suited for heavy cryptographic tasks or complex LLM inference.
